name: Audio Buffer Tuner
description: Lowers the initial TS-proxy prebuffer chunk count, and optionally the chunk size itself, for channels in a handful of chosen Channel Groups. Intended for steady, low-bitrate audio-only streams. Leave video groups unselected, since they benefit more from the default safety margin.
author: CtznSniiips

fields.label: Prebuffer chunks for matching groups
fields.help_text: Each chunk is ~256KB. Dispatcharr's normal default is 4 chunks (~1024KB) before a channel goes active. Lower values start faster but leave less margin against provider hiccups — fine for steady low-bitrate audio, riskier for video. (Shown here as a static default before the plugin is enabled; once enabled this range follows Dispatcharr's actual configured default.)

fields.label: Chunk size for matching groups (KB)
fields.help_text: Dispatcharr's normal chunk size is ~256KB. Smaller chunks mean less data has to accumulate before the first chunk (and each subsequent one) is ready, on top of whatever the prebuffer-chunk-count setting saves. Going very low increases Redis write frequency — usually fine for one or two audio channels, but don't push it to the floor across dozens of channels. Only applies to buffers created after you save this — already-running channels keep their current chunk size until they restart.

fields.label: Number of group filters
fields.help_text: How many group-picker dropdowns to show below. Increase this, save, then reload the Dispatcharr page to see the extra dropdowns.

fields.label: Group-picker dropdowns (one per filter slot, listing only Channel Groups that actually contain channels) appear here once the plugin is enabled and it can read them from the database.

actions.label: Refresh channel group options
actions.description: Re-scan Channel Groups so newly added/renamed groups are available to pick. Reload the Dispatcharr page afterward to see the change — the settings panel only loads field definitions once per page load.

actions.label: Show current status
actions.description: Reports whether the override is actually active in this process, current settings, and which Channel Groups exist — use this instead of digging through logs.
